court: High Court of Judicature at Madras
case_name: B.Sahar Banu vs The Inspector General Of Registration / on 17 October, 2022

parties.respondent_defendant: The Inspector General of Registration / The Registrar General of Marriage Registration, The District Registrar, Office of the District Registrar, Palayamkottai, Tirunelveli District, The Sub Registrar, Office of the Sub Registrar, Joint-I, Palayamkottai, Tirunelveli District, A.Abdul Hameed — husband

facts_of_case: Petitioner was forced to sign marriage register and issue certificate by her cousin who had threatened to kill her parents. She stopped going to college and informed her parents. A complaint was lodged with the Inspector of Police, Cheranmahadevi Police Station.

legal_principles.principle: The Registrar has the power to refuse registration of marriage if he is satisfied or has reason to believe that the marriage between the parties is not performed in accordance with their personal laws, custom, or usage.
legal_principles.held: As per Section 7 of the Act, the Registrar has got power to refuse the registration of marriage, if he is satisfied as reason to believe that the marriage between the parties is not performed in accordance with personal law of the parties or custom or usage or tradition.
applicable_acts_sections: Tamil Nadu Registration of Marriages Act, 2009 — Section 7

legal_principles.principle: The parties to a marriage are duty-bound to undergo the ceremonies applicable to their respective religion before registration of marriage.
legal_principles.held: A perusal of the above said provisions and Rules will clearly point out that it is mandatory for the parties to undergo those ceremonies of the marriage which are applicable to their respective religion.
applicable_acts_sections: Tamil Nadu Registration of Marriages Act, 2009 — Section 3

use_for_drafting: drafting a writ petition for divorce
seeking records in a marriage registration case
